ColigoMed, Inc.
Healthcare Interoperability & Prior Authorization Automation
www.coligomed.com

May 15, 2026
Administrator
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
Attention: CMS-0062-P
P.O. Box 8013
Baltimore, MD 21244-8013
Submitted electronically via regulations.gov

Re: CMS-0062-P — Interoperability Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs Proposed
Rule; Comment from ColigoMed, Inc.
Dear Administrator:
ColigoMed, Inc. respectfully submits the following comments in response to the Centers for
Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) proposed rule CMS-0062-P, Interoperability Standards
and Prior Authorization for Drugs (published April 14, 2026). ColigoMed is a healthcare
technology company specializing in clinical data interoperability, EHR integration, and Prior
Authorization automation. We serve physician practices, specialty groups, and health
systems across the United States, supporting providers whose patient populations are
predominantly Medicare and Medicare Advantage beneficiaries managing complex, chronic
conditions.
We strongly support CMS's continued commitment to interoperability, electronic prior
authorization, and the reduction of administrative burden on providers. We write to offer
concrete recommendations informed by our direct experience operating at the intersection of
provider workflows, payer systems, and patient care — the precise intersection that
CMS-0062-P targets.
I. ColigoMed's Perspective and Relevant Experience
ColigoMed operates at the point of care for Medicare chronic disease patients every day. Our
platform connects to provider EHR systems to identify eligible patients, enroll them in
CMS-reimbursed care programs, and coordinate continuous monitoring between office
visits. We have direct, granular visibility into the prior authorization process as it affects the
patients and providers we serve — including the delays, documentation burdens, and
clinical interruptions that CMS-0062-P seeks to address.
As a technology intermediary working with both providers and payers, we are uniquely
positioned to comment on the operational realities of implementing FHIR-based prior
authorization at scale, particularly for the chronic disease patient populations — including
those on high-cost biologics for rheumatoid arthritis, multiple sclerosis, inflammatory bowel
disease, and related conditions — who are most affected by PA delays.
II. Support for Expanding Electronic Prior Authorization to Drugs
ColigoMed strongly supports CMS's proposal to extend electronic prior authorization
requirements to cover drugs under both medical benefit and pharmacy benefit pathways.
The exclusion of drugs from CMS-0057 was widely recognized as a significant gap, and
CMS-0062-P's proposal to close it is both necessary and overdue.
From our operational experience, we observe the following regarding drug prior
authorization:
•​
Medical benefit drugs — particularly IV-administered biologics — represent some of
the highest-burden PA requests our provider-clients submit. A single biologic PA can
require 3–7 clinical documents, take 10–14 business days, and consume 4–8 hours of
staff time per submission.
•​
PA delays for these medications frequently result in clinical harm: patients on
immunomodulatory therapy for MS or IBD who experience PA-driven treatment gaps
suffer measurable disease progression.
•​
The Da Vinci CRD/DTR/PAS implementation guide framework is the right technical
approach. We have begun building against these specifications in our own platform
and can attest that they are implementable, though we note meaningful gaps in
payer readiness (addressed below).
Recommendation 2.1: Maintain the October 1, 2027 Implementation Date
We urge CMS to maintain the proposed October 1, 2027 compliance date for electronic PA
for drugs.
Recommendation 2.2: Clarify the Medical vs. Pharmacy Benefit Determination
Protocol
CMS proposes separate technical pathways for medical benefit drugs (Da Vinci FHIR) and
pharmacy benefit/Part D drugs (NCPDP protocols). We support this dual-pathway
approach, but request CMS provide clearer operational guidance on the real-time
benefit-determination step that determines which pathway applies for a given drug and
patient. In practice, this determination is a source of significant confusion and delay, and is
not addressed with sufficient specificity in the current proposed rule text.
III. FHIR Mandate: From Advisory to Required
CMS's proposal to move the Da Vinci APIs from best-practice recommendations to
mandatory requirements is a consequential and correct policy decision. ColigoMed has
observed firsthand that the advisory nature of prior interoperability guidance allowed a
significant portion of payers to defer implementation without consequence. The mandatory
framing of CMS-0062-P changes that dynamic.
Recommendation 3.1: Establish Clear Enforcement Mechanisms at Launch
The proposed rule references the National Healthcare Provider and Services Directory as an
enforcement tool — CMS can now run automated checks against published endpoints to
identify non-compliant payers. We strongly support this approach and urge CMS to publish,
at the time of final rule issuance, the specific audit methodology and enforcement
consequences for payers who fail to publish compliant endpoints. Ambiguity in enforcement
creates the conditions for non-compliance.
Recommendation 3.2: Include Technology Intermediaries in Endpoint Directory
ColigoMed and companies like us operate as authorized technology intermediaries between
providers and payers. We submit PA requests, receive prior authorization decisions, and
route clinical data on behalf of provider-clients. The proposed endpoint directory framework
focuses on payer-to-provider connectivity but does not adequately address the role of
intermediaries. We request CMS clarify how authorized intermediaries register their own
FHIR endpoints and are recognized within the directory infrastructure.
IV. Prior Authorization Reporting Requirements
CMS proposes that beginning October 1, 2027, payers must report granular prior
authorization activity data — standard versus expedited breakdowns, approval and denial
rates, and additional specificity beyond current reporting requirements. ColigoMed strongly
supports this proposal.
Recommendation 4.1: Include Drug PA in Reporting Scope from Day One
We urge CMS to confirm explicitly in the final rule that drug prior authorization is included in
the granular reporting requirements from October 1, 2027. Drug PA represents the single
highest-burden category for most physician practices. If drug PA is excluded from reporting
— even temporarily — the data will present a systematically incomplete picture of
administrative burden.
Recommendation 4.2: Make Aggregated Reporting Data Publicly Available
CMS should commit to publishing aggregated, de-identified payer PA reporting data on a
publicly accessible platform. This data would be invaluable to technology vendors, provider
organizations, and policymakers assessing where implementation friction remains highest. It
would also create market incentives for payers to improve performance before being
exposed by public reporting.
V. Implementation Considerations for Provider-Facing Platforms
As a provider-facing technology platform, ColigoMed is responsible for implementing
CMS-0062-P requirements on behalf of hundreds of physician practices that lack the
internal resources to navigate interoperability mandates independently. We offer the
following implementation observations:
•​
EHR vendor readiness varies enormously. Practices on smaller or regional EHR
platforms face significantly more implementation friction than those on Epic or
athenahealth. CMS should consider targeted technical assistance funding for
practices on non-major EHR systems.
•​
The Da Vinci CRD step — real-time coverage requirements discovery at the point of
order — is the most valuable element of the framework for providers. However, it
requires payer CDS Hooks server implementation that many payers have not yet
prioritized. CMS should monitor payer CDS Hooks readiness as a leading indicator of
overall compliance trajectory.
•​
Patient cost-sharing implications of CMS-0062-P are not fully addressed in the
proposed rule. Changes to PA requirements for drugs used by Medicare chronic
disease patients may affect patient willingness to initiate or continue treatment — an
outcome dimension CMS should model explicitly alongside administrative burden
metrics.
VI. Conclusion
ColigoMed commends CMS for the ambition and specificity of CMS-0062-P. The proposed
rule, if finalized as written, will meaningfully reduce administrative burden on physicians,
accelerate patient access to critical medications, and create a more interoperable healthcare
system. We urge CMS to maintain the October 1, 2027 implementation date, clarify
enforcement mechanisms, and extend the endpoint directory framework to recognize
authorized technology intermediaries.
ColigoMed welcomes the opportunity to provide further input, participate in technical
workgroups, or share operational data from our platform to assist CMS in implementation
planning. Please contact us at the address below.

Respectfully submitted,
Naidu Annamaneni
Chief Executive Officer
ColigoMed, Inc.
[anaidu@coligomed.com]
408.835.7454
www.coligomed.com

Submitted in response to: CMS-0062-P — Interoperability Standards and Prior
Authorization for Drugs Proposed Rule
Comment period closes: June 15, 2026
Submission method: www.regulations.gov, Docket No. CMS-0062-P

# Comment Analysis: CMS-2026-1255-0001

---

## 1. COMMENTER INFORMATION

- **Author/Organization name:** ColigoMed, Inc. - Naidu Annamaneni, Chief Executive Officer
- **Stakeholder type:** Technology Vendor
- **Credentials or expertise mentioned:** Healthcare technology company specializing in clinical data interoperability, EHR integration, and Prior Authorization automation; serves physician practices, specialty groups, and health systems; operates at the intersection of provider workflows, payer systems, and patient care; direct experience with Medicare/MA beneficiaries managing complex chronic conditions

---

## 2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

ColigoMed strongly supports CMS's proposal to expand electronic PA to drugs and make FHIR APIs mandatory, based on direct operational experience implementing PA automation at scale. The company recommends maintaining the October 1, 2027 timeline, clarifying medical vs. pharmacy benefit determination protocols, establishing clear enforcement mechanisms, including technology intermediaries in endpoint directories, and ensuring drug PA is included in reporting requirements from day one.

---

## 3. REGULATORY CONTEXT

- **Specific provisions addressed:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL, PA-DRUG-PHARMACY, FHIR-IG-REQUIRED, API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING, API-USAGE-METRICS, MEDICAL-VS-PHARMACY-BENEFIT
- **Regulatory citations mentioned:** CMS-0057 (previous rule), National Healthcare Provider and Services Directory
- **Standards referenced:** Da Vinci CRD/DTR/PAS implementation guides, FHIR, NCPDP protocols, CDS Hooks

---

## 4. DETAILED POSITIONS

**Topic 1: Expanding Electronic PA to Drugs**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL, PA-DRUG-PHARMACY
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Exclusion of drugs from CMS-0057 was significant gap. From operational experience: medical benefit drugs (especially IV biologics) represent highest-burden PA requests, requiring 3-7 clinical documents, 10-14 business days, and 4-8 staff hours per submission. PA delays cause clinical harm—patients on immunomodulatory therapy for MS/IBD suffer measurable disease progression from treatment gaps.
- **Specific request:** Finalize expansion to drugs as proposed.

**Topic 2: October 1, 2027 Implementation Date**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL, PA-DRUG-PHARMACY
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Appropriate timeline for implementation.
- **Specific request:** Maintain proposed October 1, 2027 compliance date.

**Topic 3: Medical vs. Pharmacy Benefit Determination**
- **Provision ID:** MEDICAL-VS-PHARMACY-BENEFIT
- **Position:** Support with clarification needed
- **Rationale:** Dual-pathway approach (Da Vinci FHIR for medical benefit, NCPDP for pharmacy benefit/Part D) is sound, but real-time benefit-determination step is source of significant confusion and delay in practice. Current rule text does not provide sufficient operational guidance.
- **Specific request:** Provide clearer operational guidance on benefit-determination protocol that determines which pathway applies for a given drug and patient.

**Topic 4: FHIR Mandate (Advisory to Required)**
- **Provision ID:** FHIR-IG-REQUIRED
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Advisory nature of prior interoperability guidance allowed significant portion of payers to defer implementation without consequence. Mandatory framing is consequential and correct policy decision. Da Vinci CRD/DTR/PAS framework is implementable (ColigoMed building against these specs), though gaps exist in payer readiness.
- **Specific request:** Finalize mandatory FHIR requirements as proposed.

**Topic 5: Enforcement Mechanisms**
- **Provision ID:** FHIR-IG-REQUIRED, API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING
- **Position:** Support with strengthening
- **Rationale:** National Healthcare Provider and Services Directory enables CMS to run automated checks against published endpoints to identify non-compliant payers. Ambiguity in enforcement creates conditions for non-compliance.
- **Specific request:** Publish, at time of final rule issuance, specific audit methodology and enforcement consequences for payers who fail to publish compliant endpoints.

**Topic 6: Technology Intermediaries in Endpoint Directory**
- **Provision ID:** API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING
- **Position:** Modify/Expand
- **Rationale:** ColigoMed and similar companies operate as authorized technology intermediaries, submitting PA requests and routing clinical data on behalf of provider-clients. Proposed endpoint directory focuses on payer-to-provider connectivity but does not adequately address intermediary role.
- **Specific request:** Clarify how authorized intermediaries register their own FHIR endpoints and are recognized within directory infrastructure.

**Topic 7: PA Reporting Requirements**
- **Provision ID:** API-USAGE-METRICS
- **Position:** Support with expansion
- **Rationale:** Granular PA activity data (standard vs. expedited breakdowns, approval/denial rates) is essential. Drug PA represents single highest-burden category for most physician practices. Excluding drug PA from reporting—even temporarily—would present systematically incomplete picture of administrative burden.
- **Specific request:** (1) Confirm explicitly in final rule that drug PA is included in granular reporting requirements from October 1, 2027; (2) Commit to publishing aggregated, de-identified payer PA reporting data on publicly accessible platform to create market incentives for payer performance improvement.

**Topic 8: EHR Vendor Readiness Variation**
- **Provision ID:** VENDOR-ECOSYSTEM
- **Position:** Concern
- **Rationale:** EHR vendor readiness varies enormously. Practices on smaller/regional EHR platforms face significantly more implementation friction than those on Epic or athenahealth.
- **Specific request:** Consider targeted technical assistance funding for practices on non-major EHR systems.

**Topic 9: Payer CDS Hooks Implementation**
- **Provision ID:** FHIR-IG-REQUIRED
- **Position:** Concern
- **Rationale:** Da Vinci CRD step (real-time coverage requirements discovery at point of order) is most valuable element for providers, but requires payer CDS Hooks server implementation that many payers have not yet prioritized.
- **Specific request:** Monitor payer CDS Hooks readiness as leading indicator of overall compliance trajectory.

**Topic 10: Patient Cost-Sharing Implications**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Concern
- **Rationale:** Changes to PA requirements for drugs used by Medicare chronic disease patients may affect patient willingness to initiate or continue treatment—an outcome dimension not fully addressed in proposed rule.
- **Specific request:** Model patient cost-sharing implications explicitly alongside administrative burden metrics.

---

## 5. SOLICITATION RESPONSES

The comment does not explicitly reference numbered solicitations but addresses topics covered by:

**Implicit responses:**
- **S12 (technical challenges for medical benefit drug PA APIs):** Da Vinci CRD/DTR/PAS framework is implementable based on direct build experience; notes payer readiness gaps
- **S15 (medical vs. pharmacy benefit distinction):** Supports dual-pathway but requests clearer operational guidance on real-time benefit determination
- **S21 (timeline achievable):** Urges maintaining October 1, 2027 date
- **S23-S24 (API endpoint reporting):** Supports National Healthcare Provider Directory approach; requests inclusion of technology intermediaries
- **S27 (enforcement mechanisms):** Requests specific audit methodology and enforcement consequences published at final rule issuance
- **S29-S30 (API usage metrics):** Urges explicit inclusion of drug PA from day one; recommends public aggregated data platform
- **S33 (how CMS publishes endpoints):** Recommends publicly accessible platform for aggregated payer PA data
- **S37 (implementation challenges):** Notes EHR vendor readiness variation and payer CDS Hooks gaps

---

## 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Maintain October 1, 2027 implementation date for electronic PA for drugs
2. Provide clearer operational guidance on medical vs. pharmacy benefit determination protocol
3. Publish specific audit methodology and enforcement consequences at final rule issuance
4. Clarify how authorized technology intermediaries register FHIR endpoints and are recognized in directory infrastructure
5. Confirm explicitly that drug PA is included in granular reporting requirements from October 1, 2027
6. Publish aggregated, de-identified payer PA reporting data on publicly accessible platform
7. Consider targeted technical assistance funding for practices on non-major EHR systems
8. Monitor payer CDS Hooks readiness as leading indicator of compliance
9. Model patient cost-sharing implications explicitly alongside administrative burden metrics

---

## 7. CONCERNS & OBJECTIONS

- **Primary concerns:**
  - Medical vs. pharmacy benefit determination is source of significant confusion and delay
  - Ambiguity in enforcement creates conditions for non-compliance
  - Technology intermediaries not adequately addressed in endpoint directory framework
  - Risk that drug PA could be excluded from reporting even temporarily
  - EHR vendor readiness varies enormously (smaller/regional platforms lag)
  - Many payers have not prioritized CDS Hooks server implementation
  - Patient cost-sharing implications not fully addressed

- **Potential negative impacts cited:**
  - Medical benefit drug PAs (especially IV biologics) require 3-7 documents, 10-14 days, 4-8 staff hours
  - PA delays for immunomodulatory therapy cause measurable disease progression in MS/IBD patients
  - Treatment gaps result in clinical harm
  - Implementation friction significantly higher for practices on non-major EHR systems
  - Incomplete reporting data if drug PA excluded

- **Implementation barriers mentioned:**
  - Payer readiness gaps despite implementable specifications
  - Many payers have not prioritized CDS Hooks
  - Smaller EHR platforms lack resources
  - Benefit determination protocol confusion
  - Technology intermediaries not recognized in directory framework

---

## 8. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

- **Data or statistics cited:**
  - Single biologic PA can require 3-7 clinical documents
  - Take 10-14 business days
  - Consume 4-8 hours of staff time per submission
  - Medical benefit drugs (especially IV biologics) represent highest-burden PA requests

- **Studies or research referenced:**
  - None cited

- **Examples provided:**
  - Patients on immunomodulatory therapy for MS or IBD who experience PA-driven treatment gaps suffer measurable disease progression
  - High-cost biologics for rheumatoid arthritis, multiple sclerosis, inflammatory bowel disease
  - ColigoMed's own platform build experience with Da Vinci specifications
  - Practices on Epic or athenahealth vs. smaller/regional platforms

---

## 9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

- **Affected stakeholders:**
  - Technology vendors/intermediaries
  - Physician practices (especially those on non-major EHR systems)
  - Specialty groups and health systems
  - Medicare/MA beneficiaries with complex chronic conditions
  - Patients on biologics for RA, MS, IBD
  - Payers
  - EHR vendors

- **Economic implications:**
  - Reduction in 4-8 staff hours per biologic PA submission
  - Acceleration of 10-14 day PA timelines
  - Market incentives for payer performance via public reporting
  - Need for technical assistance funding for smaller practices

- **Technical feasibility:**
  - Da Vinci CRD/DTR/PAS framework is implementable (verified through ColigoMed's build experience)
  - Payer readiness gaps exist but mandatory framing will drive compliance
  - EHR vendor readiness varies significantly
  - CDS Hooks implementation lagging at many payers

- **Patient care impact:**
  - HIGH: PA delays cause measurable disease progression in MS/IBD patients
  - Acceleration of access to critical biologics
  - Reduction in treatment gaps
  - Potential impact on patient willingness to initiate/continue treatment from cost-sharing changes

---

## 10. SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

- **Overall position:** Strongly Supportive with specific technical recommendations
- **Tone:** Professional, technically detailed, constructive, vendor-expert perspective
- **Priority level:** High

---

## 11. KEY QUOTES

1. "Medical benefit drugs — particularly IV-administered biologics — represent some of the highest-burden PA requests our provider-clients submit. A single biologic PA can require 3–7 clinical documents, take 10–14 business days, and consume 4–8 hours of staff time per submission." - Context: Establishing operational evidence for rule necessity

2. "PA delays for these medications frequently result in clinical harm: patients on immunomodulatory therapy for MS or IBD who experience PA-driven treatment gaps suffer measurable disease progression." - Context: Patient safety impact

3. "The Da Vinci CRD/DTR/PAS implementation guide framework is the right technical approach. We have begun building against these specifications in our own platform and can attest that they are implementable, though we note meaningful gaps in payer readiness." - Context: Technical feasibility assessment from vendor experience

4. "Ambiguity in enforcement creates the conditions for non-compliance." - Context: Justifying need for specific enforcement mechanisms

5. "If drug PA is excluded from reporting — even temporarily — the data will present a systematically incomplete picture of administrative burden." - Context: Advocating for drug PA inclusion in metrics from day one

---

## 12. THEMES

- [X] **IMPLEMENTATION-TIMELINE** - Strongly supports maintaining October 1, 2027 date

- [X] **COST-RESOURCES** - Notes 4-8 staff hours per biologic PA; supports technical assistance funding for smaller practices
